newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr on RBI intervention.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr on RBI intervention.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up at 35.72/73 after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars aggressively on Wednesday, dealers said.
The dollar opened the day at 35.69/70 rupees and fresh dollar inward remittances pushed up the rupee to 35.68 level.
Bouts of aggressive dollar buying by the RBI from noon turned the tide, dealers said. "They bought consistently and in lots of 10 ($10 million)," said a dealer.
One dealer said Wednesday's intervention was substantial. "I won't be surprised if they bought $100 million," he said.
There was hardly any dollar demand from any other buyer on Wednesday, dealers said.
The rupee gained in the forward dollar market tracking a fall in the domestic call money market, dealers said.
Some dealers said the RBI's dollar buying was one of the factors contributing to improved availability of rupees.
Six month annualised premia closed at 8.2 percent on Wednesday, down from the previous 8.6 percent, dealers said.
